title: Saving money to come to the United States
summary: He saved quarters in an oil can, spurred by Mario's marriage to Estela and love of New York, and left despite his family's objections.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Okay, what made you go back to singing?
Well, I put together a lot of money, to come to the United States. That's when I came to the United States.
That's right. Mario had come back to marry Estela.
In 1933 he got married with my sister.
I understand he told you about New York and everything.
But I was in love with New York without anybody....
Without anybody, huh, Macho?
I loved New York. I loved the United States.
So after he told you that, is that why you saved money, to come here?
Yes.
Okay, Macho. You were eight months over there working as administrator in your father's business. When did you decide to say, okay, I'm ready to come to New York?
By, by August, September....
Yeah. I had an oil can that I closed it and made an opening, and I used to put quarters and half a dollars in there. I had about four or five hundred dollars. It was enough money.
So all you were doing was saving money, enough money, to come to the United States.
Right.
Okay. What happened that week? Before you decided to come. Did you tell your family?
Yeah.
And then, what happened?
Oh!! They don't want me to leave Cuba. I just went by my business, went to the American consul I filled my papers and whatever, and just came to the United States.
